key_insight: High within-dataset accuracy did not ensure cross-dataset performance: held-out accuracy fell to 78.4% for EfficientNet-B0 and 66.2% for ShuffleNetV2.
clinical_relevance: The findings highlight the need for external validation before relying on MRI tumour classifiers in clinical settings.
method: Compared six deep learning architectures across four MRI classes: healthy, meningioma, glioma and pituitary tumour.
Combined four public datasets, removed exact and near-duplicates, and grouped visually similar images for 5-fold cross-validation.
Tested cross-dataset generalisation using leave-one-dataset-out evaluation.
evidence_signal: Leakage-aware cross-validation found ShuffleNetV2 (98.41%) and EfficientNet-B0 (98.23%) statistically indistinguishable (p = 0.19), but every model lost accuracy on the held-out dataset.
watch_item: Missing patient identifiers limited verification of patient-level separation; image-similarity grouping cannot guarantee its absence.
paper_title: Comparative Study of Deep Learning Architectures for Brain Tumour Classification
